notes.title: [Notice] Cheru leaving Playism
notes.content:
Hi All 

This is a general notice to all Playism titles. 
From June 14th onwards, I (Cheru) will no longer be Playism's community manager. After over 4 years of working passionately in Playism, I have decided to leave and change direction. Thank you everyone for the amazing communities you have built around Playism games and I hope that you will all continue to enjoy their games for years to come.

notes.title: YUMENIKKI -DREAM DIARY- Ver. 2.0 Release
notes.content:
Yume Nikki has been hailed as one of the greatest (and most controversial) games ever created with RPG Maker. 

YUMENIKKI -DREAM DIARY- Ver. 2.0, featuring all-new stages, expansions and updates to existing maps, and many more additional and enhanced features, is available as of May 24th, 2018.
Additionally, Ver. 2.0 is available as a free update for those who have already purchased Ver.1.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31868632/0ddbf86f9a0405f686972fe04652651d9e71c805.png[/img]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31868632/4cc0c61af117076023a04a3c72982111b50a51e3.png[/img]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/774811/YUMENIKKI_DREAM_DIARY/

[h1]YUMENIKKI -DREAM DIARY- Ver. 2.0 New Features[/h1]
[list]
    [*]Added several new areas to the game.
    [*]Added new concept art.
    [*]Added some new effects.
    [*]Mini games now save high scores when quitting.
    [*]Added audio for when the girl in the school disappears.
    [*]Added some missing effects to the mall.
    [*]Added an option to adjust the brightness of the game.
    [*]Improved performance of the eyeball wave.
    [*]Added some more secrets.
    [*]Improved AI of NPC that chases you.
[/list] 

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
[list]
    [*]Fixed NPCs in school acting as if you weren’t there when you jumped while in front of them, possibly letting you get behind them and thus causing you to get stuck.
    [*]Fixed selecting an effect in the inventory and then loading a save without that effect, causing the inventory to not auto-select an item and show the image and description from the previously selected one.
    [*]Fixed mini game pause menu not un-pausing with cancel button.
    [*]Fixed graphics menu closing sound playing at a lower volume than the rest of the items in the In-Game menu. 
    [*]Fixed a slope in the school where if you go down the stairs the player kept playing the falling animation.
    [*]Fixed a bug were if you flew above an eyeball you could remain flying in place for a while.
    [*]Fixed: In the mall NPC encounter scene some effects could be activated and deactivated while the cut scene was playing.
    [*]Effects can’t be activated anymore while having the menu opened.
    [*]Fixed a bug where after dying once, the physics would start working weirdly with the slopes.
    [*]Fixed: Pinching immediately after starting effects would leave the 3D model of the effect floating around. 
    [*]Various localization updates.
    [*]Wind zone in school resized to avoid the bug where if you open the umbrella at the end of the stairs next to the wind area she travels up while doing it.
    [*]Fixed a collider of an NPC near a house where you could go through to an unintended location.
    [*]Fixed a bug where if you interact with doors while using an effect it opened and closed fast multiple times.
    [*]Improved the stairs collider in the school.
    [*]Fixed “100%” text going outside of the frame in the diary with some languages and window sizes.
    [*]Fixed: Player could interact with triggers while being in the menu
    [*]Fixed bug where hitting the NPC that gives you the eye while running caused Madotsuki to keep running in place.
    [*]Fixed: Opening the menu in front of an active trigger that teleported Madotsuki or loaded a new location, and pressing the interaction button while in the menus would cause problems and could lock the game. 
    [*]Fixed: Closing the menu with the interaction button while in front of an interaction trigger would cause the trigger to activate unintendedly.
    [*]Fixed: Pressing pinch while taking the flute out could get you stuck until taking the flute out again.
    [*]Fixed: Could go through door in elevator room, lower floor.
    [*]Fixed: Could use the flute while waiting in the elevator, causing the input to be enabled too early.
    [*]Fixed a bug where one of the lights that explodes near an NPC kept exploding on its own.
    [*]Fixed: It was possible to skip the eye wave chasing you by running into the alley where the wave comes from at the right edge where the eyes wouldn’t touch you.
    [*]Fixed: On every scene change and when closing the in-game menu, the problem with the very high level audio was occurring when playing with very low frame rates, just like quitting to the main menu before.
    [*]Fixed: When sitting in the chair, pressing the interact button to get up would result in Madotsuki getting up and sitting down again.
    [*]Fixed: When having a controller connected, interacting with some things (like the light switch) using the keyboard would result in a duplicated interaction (e.g. the light would be turned off and on immediately).
    [*]Fixed: The places that started with an animation of Madotsuki closing the door had a problem where if you held the lantern or umbrella button you could see a floating item appearing/disappearing while the animation finished.
    [*]Other small bug fixes.
[/list]

notes.title: Wot I Think: Yume Nikki Dream Diary
notes.content:
Playing Yume Nikki: Dream Diary is like sitting across from somebody as they explain their dreams to you in great detail. No. Worse than that. It’s like listening to somebody describe an acquaintance’s dreams in great detail.

Every now and then, they pause and say something along the lines of, you had to be there , as people do when they’re telling a funny story that nobody is laughing at. In its transition from tiny sprites, abstract backgrounds and obscure free-form exploration to jerky 3d animation and side-scrolling running and jumping, Yume Nikki has lost almost all of its mysterious horror and charm.

notes.title: Yume Nikki: Dream Diary launches tomorrow
notes.content:
Time flies, eh? It feels like just a month ago that Japanese media conglomerate Kadokawa announced a successor to minimalist indie adventure Yume Nikki, working in close collaboration with Kikiyama, mysterious developer of the original game, and it’s almost here already.

Oh. It was just a month ago.

Sneaking up on us like a particularly unsettling memory of a nightmare, Yume Nikki: Dream Diary is less than a day from release. Accompanying this news is a rather unsettling trailer, painting a somewhat darker picture of protagonist Madotsuki’s dreams than anything we saw first time round.

notes.title: Free games of the week
notes.content:
Dreams, nightmares, strange worlds created in your mind. You might have heard of Yume Nikki years ago, or like me you might have only discovered it recently as it found its way onto Steam. Maybe you’re hearing about it for the first time right now, in which case you should skip down and start reading the first entry in this week’s roundup of free games.

If you have played Yume Nikki already, don t worry. I ve got plenty of other free games to recommend. Some of them are about dreams! Others are slightly creepy! And for good measure, some that are just fantastically fun to play (more…)

notes.title: Yume Nikki: Dream Diary revives cult series on Feb 23
notes.content: I hadn’t heard of Yume Nikki until a fortnight ago, when the Japanese cult classic explore-o-horror popped up on Steam after over a decade and a sequel was announced. After reading Giada Zavarise’s praise of the first one, I feel I’ve really missed something. I’m now on a timer to catch up, as the publishers today announced that sequel Yume Nikki: Dream Diary will arrive on February 23rd. It’s no longer the work of enigmatic solo creator Kikiyama but an entire team, and the sequel’s also jumping from RPG Maker’s 2D to fancy 3D. (more…)

notes.title: Announcing YumeNikki -Dream Diary-
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31717573/ef11850e91b105eb0c569857aa05fdf365a9dfc7.png[/img]

In its original form, RPG Maker darling Yume Nikki was a divisively controversial work among fans. By contrast, YumeNikki -Dream Diary- is a collaborative show of the utmost respect for auteur Kikiyama’s seminal release.

The RPG Maker team at Kadokawa has paired up with Active Gaming Media’s development team of ardent Yume Nikki fans to bring you this modern indie title in the form of YumeNikki -Dream Diary-. This diverging follow-up combines influences from the original game and other recent indie juggernauts to create something wholly unique.

notes.title: Yume Nikki s legacy: an invitation to dream
notes.content:
To see Yume Nikki appear on Steam feels like the closing of an era. This surreal game is a relic from a bygone age, when the concept of indie was still strange and the World Wide Web felt smaller, darker and more mysterious. It s the stuff dreams are made of, which is fitting, since it revolves entirely around sleeping.

(more…)

notes.title: First footage of Yume Nikki follow-up Dream Diary
notes.content:
Cult indie horror game Yume Nikki arrived on Steam this week and, more than a decade after its original release, we saw signs that the dream saga might continue. Yume Nikki is free and if you’re at all interested in wandering through subtle and not-so-subtle nightmare realms while trying to decipher their strange logic, you should play it!

A countdown site suggested we’d find out more about the new project in a couple of weeks, and now, with twelve days still to go, we have our first hints about what comes next. Dream Diary appears to be the title and the only other text says: “We can not wake up”. Oh no. I’m fairly sure there are no spoilers here because…well, you’ll see.

(more…)

notes.title: Cult horror Yume Nikki now on Steam, follow-up teased
notes.content:
I’m not a card-carrying member of the Yume Nikki cult. If I were, I’d be able to tell you how to pick your way through the dreamscape, and might even be able to decipher some of the mysteries that it contains. Since it’s original release over a decade ago, Yume Nikki has fascinated me but I’ve never spent enough time in its surreal environments to become a true acolyte. I hope there’s still room for me if I do decide to sign up because the cult of Yume Nikki is about to expand.

Yesterday, the game arrived on Steam. It’s still free, still weird as heck, but something has changed, or is about to change. Ten years on, solo developer Kikiyama is working on a sequel of sorts. Looks like we’ll know more in a couple of weeks.

(more…)
